issues.body: parse_pq_section validates the code array length but not its contents. ProductQuantizer permits K below 256, while each persisted code remains an arbitrary u8. search_slots_pq passes such a code to DistanceTable::distance, which indexes tables[s * k + c as usize] without checking c < k. Thus a crafted .spqg with a valid K=1 codebook and a code byte of 255 opens successfully but can panic in nearest(), violating the documented malformed-input fail-cleanly contract.
issues.fix_hint: While parsing the PQ section, validate every code byte against pq.k() (ideally report the slot/subspace and offending value) before constructing PqCache. Add a focused real-path test that mutates a valid persisted PQ file to use a code >= K, asserts both open and open_from_bytes return Err, and confirms no search-time panic is deferred.
issues.title: PQ sections accept out-of-range centroid codes that panic during search

verdict.summary: Round 2 fixes both prior findings: adjacency is now bounds-filtered on the real search path with mmap and owned-byte coverage, and PQ codebook size arithmetic is checked before allocation/slicing. However, the newly hardened PQ parser still accepts attacker-controlled code bytes without checking that each code is below the decoded codebook's K. Search uses those bytes directly as DistanceTable column indices, so a malformed but otherwise structurally valid PQ section can open successfully and then panic in nearest(). Because this is a new major hostile-input issue after a round with two different major findings, progress is regressing under the required scale.
